high.core: Understanding matters to you. You are energized by learning, gaining knowledge, and making sense of how things work.
high.family_expression: Within the family, you may naturally ask questions, seek context, or want to understand the reasoning behind a decision.
high.strength: This can bring curiosity, perspective, and thoughtful problem-solving.
high.watchout: You may sometimes want more explanation than another family member feels is necessary.

low.core: You are less likely to need extensive explanation or knowledge before something becomes useful to you.
low.family_expression: Within the family, you may be comfortable moving forward once you have enough information rather than continuing to study the issue.
low.strength: This can support practical decision-making and reduce unnecessary analysis.
low.watchout: A highly Intellectual family member may occasionally feel that an issue is being resolved before it has been fully understood.

high.core: You tend to trust experience, intuition, and what has already proven useful rather than needing extensive theory.
high.family_expression: You may often approach family decisions through what feels practical or familiar.
high.strength: This can help simplify decisions and keep attention on what actually works.
high.watchout: Highly Intellectual family members may sometimes want more analysis or explanation than you naturally require.

low.core: Instinctive considerations are less likely to dominate your decisions.
low.family_expression: You may be more willing to investigate, learn, or challenge familiar assumptions before deciding what makes sense.
low.strength: This can support curiosity and openness to new information.
low.watchout: There may be times when additional analysis adds complexity to something another person sees as straightforward.

high.core: You tend to pay close attention to usefulness, efficiency, resources, and return on effort.
high.family_expression: At home, you may naturally ask whether a decision produces a meaningful result or makes good use of time, money, or energy.
high.strength: This can bring practical judgment and strong stewardship of resources.
high.watchout: Not every family decision is best evaluated primarily through efficiency or measurable return.

low.core: Practical return is less likely to be the central reason something matters to you.
low.family_expression: You may be willing to invest in something because of its personal or relational value even when the practical payoff is difficult to measure.
low.strength: This can make room for experiences and priorities that are valuable without being efficient.
low.watchout: A highly Resourceful family member may occasionally wonder why practical implications are receiving less attention.

high.core: You may be relatively willing to contribute time, effort, or resources without requiring a direct personal return.
high.family_expression: Within the family, you may naturally support needs simply because helping feels worthwhile.
high.strength: This can bring generosity and willingness to contribute without keeping score.
high.watchout: Without healthy boundaries, generosity can sometimes become overextension.

low.core: You are less likely to separate effort completely from the value or outcome it produces.
low.family_expression: You may naturally consider whether an investment of time or resources makes sense before committing.
low.strength: This can protect against overcommitment or poorly defined obligations.
low.watchout: More Selfless family members may sometimes experience this practical evaluation as overly transactional.

high.core: You tend to value experience, balance, surroundings, and a sense that life feels personally meaningful.
high.family_expression: You may be especially attentive to atmosphere, quality of experience, and whether family life feels balanced.
high.strength: This can bring sensitivity to environment, experience, and quality of life.
high.watchout: Highly practical family members may sometimes place less weight on atmosphere or experience than you do.

low.core: Experience or aesthetic balance is less likely to outweigh practical considerations.
low.family_expression: You may focus more readily on what needs to be accomplished than on whether the process feels ideal.
low.strength: This can help maintain focus when conditions are imperfect.
low.watchout: Family members who strongly value experience or harmony may occasionally feel that atmosphere is being overlooked.

high.core: You tend to place greater emphasis on functionality and observable results than on atmosphere or aesthetic experience.
high.family_expression: You may naturally focus on whether something works rather than whether it feels ideal.
high.strength: This can bring practicality and clarity when circumstances are messy.
high.watchout: A highly Harmonious family member may want greater attention paid to the experience surrounding the outcome.

low.core: Pure functionality is less likely to be enough by itself when evaluating an experience or decision.
low.family_expression: You may care not only about what happens, but also about how the environment or experience feels.
low.strength: This can support greater attention to quality of life and personal experience.
low.watchout: Practical family members may occasionally see those considerations as secondary.

high.core: You tend to place meaningful value on helping, supporting, and improving outcomes for other people.
high.family_expression: Within the family, you may naturally notice who needs support and feel motivated to contribute to their well-being.
high.strength: This can bring empathy, generosity, and strong concern for others.
high.watchout: A strong desire to help can occasionally make it difficult to recognize when another person needs independence rather than assistance.

low.core: Helping others is less likely to become an automatic priority simply because a need exists.
low.family_expression: You may be more selective about when, where, and how you invest support.
low.strength: This can protect boundaries and encourage personal responsibility.
low.watchout: Highly Altruistic family members may sometimes experience that selectivity as a lack of concern even when that is not the intention.

high.core: You tend to be selective about where your time, support, and attention are invested.
high.family_expression: You may naturally consider purpose, boundaries, and intended outcomes before becoming involved.
high.strength: This can create focus and reduce indiscriminate overcommitment.
high.watchout: A highly Altruistic family member may sometimes prefer helping first and evaluating limits later.

low.core: Strict selectivity is less likely to determine whether you become involved in supporting others.
low.family_expression: You may be relatively open to responding when someone needs assistance.
low.strength: This can make you accessible and responsive to people around you.
low.watchout: Without clear boundaries, responsiveness can occasionally become overextension.

high.core: You tend to value influence, direction, independence, and the ability to shape outcomes.
high.family_expression: Within the family, you may naturally want a meaningful voice in decisions and feel energized when you can affect what happens next.
high.strength: This can bring leadership, confidence, and willingness to take responsibility.
high.watchout: Other family members may sometimes need influence over the process even when you already see a clear direction.

low.core: Personal control or authority is less likely to be a central source of motivation.
low.family_expression: You may be comfortable contributing without needing to determine the final direction.
low.strength: This can support flexibility and shared decision-making.
low.watchout: Highly Commanding family members may occasionally occupy more leadership space than you intended to give them.

high.core: You tend to value shared participation, collective contribution, and working with others toward outcomes.
high.family_expression: You may naturally prefer family decisions that allow people to contribute rather than concentrating influence in one person.
high.strength: This can support inclusion, teamwork, and shared ownership.
high.watchout: Collaboration can sometimes take longer than a more individually driven family member considers necessary.

low.core: Collective participation is less likely to be required before you feel comfortable moving forward.
low.family_expression: You may be relatively comfortable with individual ownership and clearly defined decision authority.
low.strength: This can create speed and accountability.
low.watchout: Highly Collaborative family members may occasionally want more involvement in decisions than you naturally expect.

high.core: You tend to value established systems, consistency, principles, and clear frameworks.
high.family_expression: Within the family, you may prefer expectations, routines, or decisions to have a recognizable structure behind them.
high.strength: This can create consistency, clarity, and dependable standards.
high.watchout: A strongly Receptive family member may sometimes experience established structure as unnecessarily restrictive.

low.core: Established systems or traditions are less likely to receive automatic preference simply because they already exist.
low.family_expression: You may be willing to reconsider routines or rules when another approach appears more useful.
low.strength: This can create adaptability and openness to change.
low.watchout: Highly Structured family members may need greater consistency than you naturally require.

high.core: You tend to be open to new approaches, alternatives, and changing established methods when circumstances justify it.
high.family_expression: You may naturally question whether an existing family routine is still the best way to handle something.
high.strength: This can bring adaptability, experimentation, and openness to improvement.
high.watchout: Highly Structured family members may sometimes experience that flexibility as instability or unnecessary change.

low.core: Constantly reconsidering established approaches is less likely to be motivating for you.
low.family_expression: You may prefer consistency when an existing structure continues to work.
low.strength: This can support stability and continuity.
low.watchout: More Receptive family members may occasionally want greater freedom to experiment or redefine the process.

clusters.primary: These are the motivations most likely to consistently capture your attention and influence your decisions.
clusters.situational: These motivations remain available to you, but their importance is more likely to depend on the circumstances.
clusters.indifferent: These motivations generally carry less weight in determining why you choose one direction over another.

closing: Driving Forces become especially useful in family dynamics because two people can agree on what should happen while being motivated by completely different reasons.
Understanding those differences makes it easier to distinguish disagreement about the goal from disagreement about what makes the goal worth pursuing.
